name: NGC 3432, SN 2000ch field (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 3432, a galaxy home to the supernova impostor SN 2000ch, seen by Hubble.
label: sn2000ch-hubble
story: SN 2000ch was never a true supernova but an impostor: a luminous blue variable star that keeps erupting. Its outbursts repeat on a regular beat, perhaps driven by violent close passes in an eccentric binary.

claims.text: SN 2000ch is a supernova impostor in NGC 3432
Its eruptions come from a luminous blue variable star
The outbursts repeat periodically, possibly from interaction at periastron in an eccentric binary
Host NGC 3432, type Impostor, observed in GO-16179 in F555W and F814W
Hubble program 16179 imaged the site of SN 2000ch
